note: P07 D6 / P14 D3. Every entry is a fact about a shape that is *not* a secret, with the reason written here rather than as a grep exclusion nobody can see. `tools/ci-log-scan.py --sources` and `tools/p14-appsec-scan.py` both read this file; the scan prints how many lines it skipped.

paths.why: captured venue fixtures: condition ids, token ids and tx hashes are public identifiers and have the 64-hex shape
phase documents and recorded evidence quote command output, which contains ids, hashes and redacted material
static assets; nothing secret is inlined at build time by design (P08)
vendored third-party skill reference docs: example credentials in prose, never imported by the product

strings.why: tools/repo-recover.sh builds the remote URL from a shell variable read out of ~/.secrets/tokens.env; the interpolation is the safe form, and this is the line someone writes during an incident
the dev compose DSN, with the dev-only password written down next to it in the same file

the Telegram test constant (tests/test_telegrambot.py and two siblings). It is built to satisfy the verifier's *shape* check and carries a `# lint-allow: shape only, never a real token` marker at the tip; this entry exists because history scanning reads the commit where the constant had no marker yet
the second shape-valid Telegram fixture token, used to prove a token signed by another bot is refused
a fixture referral code in the web tests (a real code is 22 chars of `secrets.token_urlsafe`; this one is the alphabet), marked at the tip

the *planted* fake AWS key in tools/p07-gate-check.py's log-scan table: the check asserts the scanner finds it. It is deliberately not a valid key shape (no key material, 16 chars of A-Z) and it appears only in that assertion
the redact/log-scan self-test's PEM vector: the header plus a two-line body, quoted as the string the scanner must catch. A real leaked PEM line does not have this assignment in front of it
the same vector in tools/p07-gate-check.py's own table

the redactor's PEM fixture inside tests/test_security_plane.py's table of shapes `redact_text` must mask. The `\nabc\n` body is what makes it unmistakably a fixture rather than key material, and the line carries `# lint-allow: fixture` at the tip; this entry covers the commit before that marker existed

the password-shaped literal that `tools/p14-appsec-scan.py` plants in a throwaway file to prove its SAST rule set actually fires — the canary has to look like the thing the rules catch, so it *must* be a fake credential. It appears in history because an earlier commit of that scanner carried the line before the `# lint-allow: the canary this scanner must catch` marker was added to it
